title: Everton insider reveals update on David Moyes quitting the club - 'I know him well'
content: David Moyes could walk away from Everton if he is not backed by The Friedkin Group in the January transfer window. That is according to former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who does not see him quitting the club unless further fall-outs take place. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Moyes has been vocal in his disappointment at the outcome of Everton's whirlwind summer transfer window. The Toffees have been left with just 18 senior, outfield players after failing to bolster his squad in several different positions. He will be working with that small group of players until January at least, when Everton must back him with several new additions. If that does not happen, then Moyes may well see fit to quit as the Toffees manager and take another job. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement David Moyes' Everton exit prediction issued after summer saga Everton's former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy advising elite clubs – thinks several clubs could be interested in hiring Moyes in the new year. He does not want to leave Everton just yet, but will stand by his principles and potentially walk out if the club does not boost his squad in January. Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained: "There's no way. I don't see David doing that. David doesn't bluff, he doesn't play games. I know him well, obviously, from our time together at Everton, which was a very successful period. He loves the club, and when he said to the fans that their manager is an Evertonian, he can actually say that and know it's true. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I don't see him walking away yet, but I think January is going to be quite important, because if he isn't backed again then, I think everybody would understand if he was to move on. David's stock is pretty high right now and I think there would be other suitors at that time of the season." Everton 'concerned' about James Garner after rivals 'turn his head' Everton concerned about James Garner's future There are plenty of question marks lingering over Everton right now, and Moyes' future is not their only concern. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Sources have exclusively revealed to Football Insider that Everton are worried that star midfielder Garner could be poached by a bigger club in the next 12 months. Chelsea reportedly saw a late approach for his services rejected by Everton on Deadline Day, although Moyes denied any contact between the two clubs. His performances under the Scot have attracted acclaim over the last two seasons, and he earned a maiden England call-up in March.

title: Harsh Goenka proposes N. Chandrasekaran to help shape India's AI strategy
content: Harsh Goenka, Chairman of RPG Enterprises, proposed on September 7 that Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran could help guide India's national artificial intelligence strategy and its execution. The suggestion, made in a post on X, comes as India accelerates investment in AI infrastructure and faces decisions about who will steer that expansion at a policy level. The proposal and its precedents Goenka pointed to earlier instances where private-sector executives took on public responsibilities. He cited Nandan Nilekani, who led the Unique Identification Authority of India and the Aadhaar programme, and Pawan Goenka, the former Mahindra & Mahindra managing director who now chairs IN-SPACe, India's space sector regulator. "India brought Nandan Nilekani from private sector to lead Aadhaar/UIDAI and now educational reforms and Pawan Goenka to help drive our space ambitions through IN-SPACe," Goenka wrote. He then asked, "Why not tap N. Chandrasekaran's (Tatas) experience to help shape India's AI strategy and implementation?" No formal government role for Chandrasekaran has been announced. Goenka's post did not specify a particular position, and there is no indication that the government has extended any such proposal to the Tata Sons chairman. Chandrasekaran's technology track record Chandrasekaran joined Tata Consultancy Services in the 1980s and rose to become its chief executive before assuming the chairmanship of Tata Sons. Under his leadership, the group has expanded into semiconductor manufacturing, electronics, data centres, and digital infrastructure. His public comments on AI align with the scale of the challenge. At the India AI Impact Summit in February, he described artificial intelligence as the next major infrastructure. "AI to my mind is the next big infrastructure. It is the infrastructure of intelligence," he said, comparing the shift to earlier transformations driven by electricity, steam engines, and the internet. He also emphasised broad access. "Our mission should be to make AI work for every individual and every citizen in this country," Chandrasekaran said. Mixed reactions to a corporate role in policy Responses to Goenka's post were divided. Some users supported tapping Chandrasekaran's experience for economic planning beyond AI alone. Others suggested that Nandan Nilekani, given his work on Aadhaar and public technology platforms, would be better suited to lead AI transformation. One comment floated Anand Mahindra as a candidate for strengthening Brand India, while another questioned whether individual-sector specialists should drive technology policy at all. The debate highlights a persistent tension in India's technology governance: when to bring private-sector leaders into national planning roles and how to define the scope of their influence. For executives watching this space, the discussion signals that India's AI policy framework is still taking shape, and the question of leadership remains open. Why this matters for executives and strategy The conversation Goenka started is not about one individual. It surfaces a strategic question that affects anyone building or buying AI systems in India: who will set the standards, procurement rules, and infrastructure priorities that shape the market. When a corporate chair with Chandrasekaran's operational scale is named as a potential architect of national AI strategy, it suggests that implementation experience - not just policy expertise - may carry weight in the rooms where decisions get made. For strategy leaders, tracking who gets the mandate matters as much as tracking the technology itself. The AI for Executives & Strategy implications extend to procurement planning, partnership decisions, and compliance readiness. Professionals involved in governance should also watch how public-private role definitions evolve, a topic covered in the AI Learning Path for Policy Makers.

title: Pinarayi Vijayan defends daughter Veena, says all payments accounted for
content: Pinarayi Vijayan defended his daughter Veena amid allegations related to her company's transactions with CMRL. He said all payments were accounted for, taxes were paid, and dismissed allegations of money being routed through her husband, Muhammad Riyas. Former Keralam Chief Minister and State Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan on Wednesday defended his daughter Veena Vijayan amid allegations related to transactions involving her company and Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL), saying all payments were properly accounted for and taxes were paid. "My daughter is a young woman working in the computer sector. To me, she is still a child. After completing her studies, she worked at Oracle, a world-famous IT company. She left the job when continuing it after marriage became difficult. In the meantime, she has worked in foreign countries as well. Had she continued there, she would have grown to a very high salary scale. Following that, an attempt was made to start her own company. That company provides services to many people. It provides services to many establishments. At one point, a news report I used to hear was that those receiving the services included religious extremists. That there were institutions of religious extremists. It is a very famous charitable trust," he said "Among that group was the transaction that took place with the CMRL company. The remuneration paid in the transaction with my daughter's company was not a secret matter. That is a matter concerning companies. Accurate taxes have been paid for all of that. Everything has proper accounting and records. At one point, this was raised as an allegation. At that point, Muhammad Riyas was not Veena's husband," Vijayan said. Vijayan rejects allegations against son-in-law Muhammad Riyas He also rejected allegations that money received by Veena was later routed through her husband, Muhammad Riyas, and questioned whether media reports could make him a bribe-taker. "What the media reports is that money was received for me. That money was funnelled out by Veena through Riyas. The ED found that money received by Veena years ago was funnelled through her husband Riyas years later. As if Veena had kept that money safe all these years. Just because you printed it in bold headlines, will I turn into a bribe-taker in front of the people of Kerala? Personal life is not something that shatters just because you print headlines to vent your anger, revenge, and hatred. Do not start all this thinking you can break us with it. It will be faced politically and legally. What needs to be faced politically will be faced politically, and what needs to be faced legally will be faced legally," he said. ED action a political hunt: Vijayan On the Enforcement Directorate's request to the Kerala Police to register an FIR against him and Muhammad Riyas, Vijayan said the action against him was part of an attempt to implicate him. "The hunting against me did not start all of a sudden. Things have not progressed as desired by the forces that tried against me. Now the ED is making decisions. One morning, they entered the house I was living in. Their intention is clear to everyone. They need to frame or blame me in some way. They are not getting anything helpful for that," he said. The CMRL Controversy The controversy arose after the Company of Veena, M/s Exalogic Solutions Private Limited (a one-person company), allegedly received fraudulent payments totalling Rs 2.78 crore from CMRL under the guise of IT Consultancy Services. Further M/s Empower India Capital Investment Private Limited (EICPL), operated by Sasidharan Kartha, Managing Director of CMRL, extended loans to Exalogic totalling Rs. 50 Lakh, despite Exalogic failing to make timely repayments, the ED said in a release. The agency further claimed that the investigations done by the ED before showed that Proceeds of Crime were generated by the management of CMRL led by SN Sasidharan Kartha and bribes were paid to various persons. Veena is allegedly one of the recipients of money from CMRL without rendering any services. (ANI)

title: Property consultancy relocates amid growth
content: Property consultancy relocates amid growth A property regeneration consultancy has relocated its Newcastle office following five years of growth across the North East. AspinallVerdi has moved its team from The Core at Newcastle Helix to Grainger Hub on Grainger Street, providing additional space to support its expanding regional operation. The relocation comes five years after the independent consultancy established a presence in Newcastle and follows growth across its regeneration, development and advisory services. During that period, the team has worked on public and private sector regeneration, development and placemaking projects for clients including Homes England, Northumberland Council, Darlington Council, Taylor Wimpey, Vinci Developments and Gentoo Group. Its expansion has also been supported by the recent appointment of Laurence Trevor on a year-out placement from Northumbria University, as the business looks to develop future talent within the region’s property sector. Bosses say the new city centre base will improve connectivity and accessibility for clients and partners while providing capacity for further growth as demand for its regeneration, development and valuation services increases. Brett Devenish, director and head of the Newcastle office of AspinallVerdi, said: “Identifying and securing a well-located new office such as Grainger Hub, builds on the success of our five years in Newcastle, and with the appointment of Laurence we’re well positioned to continue our growth trajectory.” Founded in 2009 by executive chairman Atam Verdi and managing director Ben Aspinall, AspinallVerdi employs more than 30 people. Alongside its Leeds headquarters and Newcastle operation, the consultancy has offices in Liverpool, Manchester, Birmingham and London, providing property regeneration advice to public and private sector clients nationwide. title: China Focus: China services trade fair showcases innovation, promotes openness
content: BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) opened Wednesday in Beijing, as China steps up efforts to expand opening-up in services trade at the outset of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Running through Sept. 13 at Shougang Park, a former industrial site and venue for the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics, the fair has drawn participants from 90 countries, regions and international organizations, with over 1,800 companies exhibiting on-site. Among them are 473 Fortune Global 500 firms and other industry leaders, including Honeywell, Johnson & Johnson and Siemens. Themed "Global Services, Shared Prosperity," this year's CIFTIS features a Global Trade in Services Summit, co-hosted by China's Ministry of Commerce and the Beijing municipal government, together with the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development and the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO). A series of forums and business matchmaking activities will also be held during the fair. During the summit, Zimbabwean Vice President Constantino Chiwenga said the CIFTIS is expected to create many investment opportunities across conferencing, exhibition, infrastructure, and digital services, adding that it will help Zimbabwe identify opportunities for trade in services, build export capacity, and attract credible partners across technology, finance, tourism, education and health care. Alexander Poulev, deputy prime minister and minister of Economy, Investment and Industry of Bulgaria, said at the summit that trade in services is an important pillar of the China-Bulgarian relationship. "We want to see more Bulgarian products reaching the Chinese market and more Bulgarian companies building long-term partnerships with Chinese businesses," he said. More than 100 new products and services will make their debut at the fair, covering fields such as information and communications, fintech, and digital and intelligent healthcare. Another highlight is a new overseas expansion services roadshow area, which offers Chinese companies one-stop professional support to enter foreign markets and expand the global footprint of Chinese services. "Going global today is no longer just about competitive pricing, but also about adapting to different rules, managing compliance and navigating risks," said Li Yao from KPMG China, adding that the new service area comes at an opportune time. The core exhibition area also debuts a showcase of more than 140 innovation cases spanning all 12 categories of services trade, including artificial intelligence, large language models, and intelligent agents, offering a glimpse of where China's services sector is headed. Advancing trade in services and promoting opening up and cooperation in the services sector is not only China's choice but also a global necessity, Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang said in a keynote speech at the summit. He noted China's efforts in actively promoting trade in services and opening up its services sector wider, which are creating more opportunities for countries and businesses around the world. The fair itself offered a glimpse of that openness in action. Norway, this year's guest country of honor, presented a pavilion featuring a wide range of exhibits, including health and nutrition, green transition, and design and lifestyle. Henning Kristoffersen, commercial counselor of the Norwegian Embassy in Beijing, said the opportunity allows Norway to show a much broader picture of its commercial relationship with China. "What we want to do at CIFTIS is to broaden it further into services, technology, culture and knowledge-based cooperation," he said. China is Norway's largest trading partner in Asia, with around 160 Norwegian companies operating in China, he added. Klaus Hoseth, CEO of Hoseth Technology, a Norwegian fish-processing technology firm, is attending CIFTIS for the first time and looking to cooperate with Chinese robotics and AI companies. "We hope to improve automation and efficiency in our production line, and leverage Chinese open-source AI technologies to make factory systems smarter," he said. He also noted the strong potential for cooperation between China's vast market and Norway's marine food industry. The interest shown by international participants comes as China's services trade continues to grow. China has posted rapid growth in services trade, with strong exports of knowledge-intensive services supported by the country's IP and innovation ecosystem, said WIPO Director General Daren Tang in his video address to the summit. Latest official data showed that in the first seven months of 2026, China's services trade totaled nearly 4.45 trillion yuan (about 656.6 billion U.S. dollars), up 8.3 percent year on year. A report released at CIFTIS on Wednesday also highlighted the growing strength of China's services brands. China ranks second globally with 21 brands in the world's 100 most valuable trade in services brands, with a combined worth of 876.8 billion U.S. dollars, according to the report titled "Trade in Services 100 2026" released by Brand Finance, a leading brand valuation consultancy. Advancing high-quality development of services trade is a key task in the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), which calls for intensified efforts to optimize negative list management of services trade, ease cross-border restrictions, encourage services exports, and foster knowledge-intensive services trade. ■

title: City Council nears completion of 2027 budget, expands taxi stand parking
content: About $3.2 million in changes were made to Columbia's proposed 2027 fiscal year budget Tuesday night as the Columbia City Council put the finishing touches on the document during a regular meeting. The council also approved a plan to nearly double the number of downtown parking spaces cordoned off at night for taxis, Uber and Lyft vehicles, and approved new waste disposal rates. The budget covers expenditures and revenues for fiscal year 2027, which begins Oct. 1. The council, which has held three public hearings during the past month to give residents an opportunity to comment on the budget, is expected to cast a final vote on the budget during its next regular meeting Sept. 21. In all, the council on Tuesday proposed around $940,000 in additional expenditures to include in the budget. It also struck down an amendment allocating $7,000 to reimburse council members up to $1,000 each annually for home security systems. That amendment came at the request of Third Ward council member Jacque Sample, who told the Missourian last month that she and other council members — all of whom are women — had experienced sexism and harassment on social media. But other council members disagreed that it would be a good use of city funds. “I agree that we are seeing personal attacks and threats. And we're not the first, and we certainly won't be the last, and I don't know that any of them are any more credible than any of the ones that we've seen in the past,” Fourth Ward council member Sharon Geuea Jones said. “I personally would not want any city equipment in my home.” The vote to approve security reimbursements for council members failed 2-4, with Mayor Barbara Buffaloe and Sample voting for it, and Sixth Ward council member Betsy Peters absent. The council also approved an additional $200,000 for the Utilities Assistance Program, which is no longer supported by federal COVID-19 pandemic-era American Rescue Plan Act funding. City staff members had earlier proposed that the city cut back its assistance program, which without federal funding relies mostly on donations from utility customers to help those in need. The fiscal year 2027 budget does not yet include the revenue from Proposition 1, a one-cent public safety sales tax approved by voters in August that is projected to generate roughly $38 million annually for police and fire services. Revenue from Proposition 1 will not be collected until Jan. 1, and the city will not begin receiving funds from it until March, city officials have said. The council also approved an amended budget for fiscal year 2026, which concludes on Sept. 30. The adjustments consist of $11.8 million in new funding and $6.2 million in re-appropriated funds from other projects. The council typically makes adjustments to its current year budget each quarter. The adjusted budget includes $7.2 million in electric expenditures, about $3.62 million in street and sidewalk improvements and $1.16 million in Columbia Fire Department funding, among other city projects and funds. New ride-sharing spots downtown The council approved a plan to nearly double the number of metered parking spots reserved for taxi, Uber and Lyft pickups in the downtown area. Since last summer, the city has cordoned off certain 34 downtown parking spots at night to make room for taxis and services such as Uber and Lyft to pick up riders. The number of spots is being increased to 66. “This is a common-sense measure to help us with traffic control,” First Ward council member Valerie Carroll said. Assistant Police Chief Mark Fitzgerald told the council that with patron behaviors turning more toward using ride-sharing services and taxis both for downtown arrivals and departures, the taxi/ride-share stands would operate beginning at 9 p.m., rather than the current 11 p.m. start time. Food and package delivery drivers will also be able to use the pickup areas. Users will have a 15-minute loading or unloading limit. The areas where metered spots are cordoned off will be along portions of Broadway and Cherry, Walnut, Ninth and Tenth streets. “The main objectives of the ordinance is to reduce traffic congestion, illegal stopping, double parking, and just increase overall pedestrian safety in the downtown entertainment area,” Fitzgerald said. "We want to make ride shares, I think, in the city more attractive for patrons and users too.” Waste disposal The council also approved changes to the rates residents and businesses pay for disposing liquid waste and using the city’s sewer system. The amendments to Chapter 13 of the city code will increase the amount charged for the removal of sludge from treatment plants, according to a staff report. The amendments will also increase the amount charged for the removal of waste in portable/chemical toilets, domestic holding tanks, septic tanks and other wastewater storage vessels and eliminate a $12.37 fee per truck load for waste haulers. The amendments to Chapter 22 will decrease the base charge and increase the volume charge for all customers. They will also increase the sewer connection fee based on the size of the water meter required to serve the property. “So users will see a change in the monthly bill. The residential base charge will be going down to $11.10 per month, and the volume charge per (hundred cubic feet) will be going up to $2.68,” Utilities Director Erin Keys said. “So generally, if you use 9 CCF or less water each month, but it's discharged into your sewer, your monthly bill will go down.” Other approved changes in wastewater treatment and removal costs will only affect certain industries and businesses. A study conducted by the consultancy firm Stantec recommended that the city increase wastewater system rates by 3.25% for each fiscal year from 2028 to 2036. Council will vote on these increases in coming years. Other action The council also swore in Michael Parks as the first director of the city’s new Airport Department. The City Council also heard comments from members of the public who spoke about urban camping and police enforcement. Additionally, the council approved a price increase for the ParkLync Downtown Employee Permit Program from $35 per month to $40 per month. The permits are valid for 10-hour, on-street parking meters. The initial amendment proposed increasing the fee to $50 per month, but the council voted to decrease the approved change. The council struck down an amendment that would limit commercial businesses, organizations, property owners and affiliated entities to five Special Event Permits annually. The amendment would have also clarified the purpose of the Special Event Permit process.

title: Bolivian bot farms fuel right-wing takeover of Latin America
content: Fernando Cerimedo, then an 'advisor' to the National Party, points at a map of Honduras during presidential candidate Nasry Asfura's press conference in Tegucigalpa, Honduras, Dec. 1, 2025. | Moises Castillo / AP The sound of gunfire erupted outside a hotel in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, the epicenter of right-wing politics in Bolivia, on the evening of Aug. 17. By the time the commotion was over, a woman lay on the ground with three bullets in her, and within hours, the entire country was plunged into political scandal. Two hitmen disguised as delivery drivers shot and nearly killed lawyer Nadia Beller, but they failed to finish the job. Hospitalized, she talked with reporters and police—and what she revealed triggered the arrest, the very next day, of her partner, political operative Fernando Cerimedo. Beller, a former parliamentary candidate, had worked in the socialist MAS government of Evo Morales (2007-19). Recently, though, she served as an advisor in the conservative, U.S.-supported government of President Rodrigo Paz, elected on Nov. 8, 2025. Beller described Cerimedo as angry “about her pregnancy.” However, it was what she said next that set off an avalanche of investigations. Cerimedo, accord to Beller, was “concerned about her knowledge of illegal activities he was carrying out…[in various] countries, to promote conservative politicians and attack progressives.” Quickly, it became apparent that her accusations lined up with messages on Cerimedo’s phone reviewed by investigators. They found at his residence “hundreds of thousands of dollars” and computer equipment used to run a “bot farm.” A massive criminal inquiry is now underway, but the charges so far include attempted murder, domestic abuse, illicit enrichment, and narcotrafficking. The attack on Beller, however, pulled back the curtain on a far larger story. It’s now apparent that Cerimedo and several associates have been engaged in an extended campaign of media disinformation that helped drive the recent election victories of extreme right-wing presidential candidates across Latin America. Cerimedo took the lead, serving the wealthy and politically powerful across the region and farther afield in a massive digital communications and deception operation. U.S. influence, it seems, was lurking in the background during it all. Bolivian bots Under interrogation, Cerimedo claimed he worked as an unpaid adviser in Paz’s government. His office adjoined that of the president. He told investigators that “outside consulting work” provides him with $1 million per year, or per month; his accounts varied. His importance to Paz shows in a photo of Secretary of State Marco Rubio conferring with president at the Shield of the Americas Summit in Miami in March—with Cerimedo at his side. Cerimedo’s value went beyond the role of adviser, though, as it now looks as though his bot farm was working overtime to shape Bolivian opinion prior to Paz’s electoral victory in 2025. A bot farm, as described by journalist Miguel Ángel San Martín, “is a network of many accounts or devices controlled automatically to generate fake likes, followers, comments, or views; to post or amplify messages en masse on social media; to click on ads or manipulate polls; to automatically create accounts; and to engage in spamming, fraud, or attempts to overwhelm [electronic] services. They are…extremely difficult to detect.” It wasn’t only in his home country of Bolivia, however, that he put his operation to work. Voting undermined in Honduras Cerimedo’s central role in determining the outcome of Honduras’s recent presidential election came to light in August following his arrest. There, the social democratic Libre Party held power prior to presidential voting on Nov. 30, 2025. Shortly before the election, Marlon Ochoa, Libre’s representative on the National Election Council, publicized leaked audio recordings of conversations of the National and Liberal Parties’ representatives. They were insisting that delivery of ballots and the count should be delayed but simultaneously called for the announcement of victory for their preferred candidates well before all votes were tallied. That’s precisely what happened; hundreds of thousands of votes were never counted. In the meantime, millions of text messages lit up phones across the country warning that remittances would not arrive from the U.S. if the Libre Party’s Rixi Moncada won. Prior to the voting, President Donald Trump released Juan Orlando Hernández, Honduras’s former president for the National Party, from a U.S. prison where he had been serving 43 years for drug trafficking. National Party candidate Nasry Asfura had placed third in opinion polls, but suddenly he was Honduras’s new president. On Aug. 26, Marlon Ochoa, the former national election councilor currently living in exile, reported that Fernando Cerimedo’s voice was heard on the leaked audio recordings he delivered to the attorney general’s office in December 2025. There, Cerimedo talked about stuffing votes for Asfura into ballot boxes, discarding votes, and not accepting a “vote-by-vote recount.” In Chile Cerimedo tried to disrupt the 2020 Chilean referendum on a new constitution that would have replaced one inherited from the Pinochet dictatorship. Socialist parliamentarian Juan Santana claimed recently that Cerimedo’s own consultancy firm had staged an opinion poll aimed at falsely showing that the “Yes” vote was losing ground. (It passed by 78%.) Cerimedo supported the “Reject” option. Santana accuses three officials in the government of current right-wing President José Antonio Kast of cooperating with Cerimedo in that endeavor. He claims that bots let loose by Cerimedo eased candidate Kast’s path to electoral victory in 2025 and also that “artificial accounts and trolls” disparaged progressive presidential candidate Evelyn Matthei. In Peru The results of second-round presidential voting in Peru on June 7 were close. According to elciudadano.com, right-wing candidate Keiko Fujimori had included “Cerimedo as one of her main electoral campaign advisors.” In the first round of voting, “Cerimedo’s network…began to operate covertly in the country through bots, trolls, and false content.” He “launched a disinformation campaign against progressive candidate Roberto Sánchez,” who was ahead in the polls. Ultimately, “the dirty work of Cerimedo” was decisive in overcoming Sánchez’s lead. To be able to intervene in Peru, Cerimedo and Spanish journalist Javier Negre (see below) built a relationship with Carlos Díaz-Rosillo, who has served in two Trump administrations, in the White House and then the Department of Defense. The Department’s website proclaims that Díaz-Rosillo advises Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth “in all matters related to defense policy and strategy in the Western Hemisphere.” Díaz-Rosillo and Keiko Fujimori are acquainted. In 2025, Díaz-Rosillo honored her at the Florida-based Adam Smith Center, which he founded and directed. Fujimori must have been appreciative; she had only recently emerged from a failed prosecution on money-laundering charges. Accepting Díaz-Rosillo’s recommendation of Cerimedo, she might have been returning the favor. In Colombia Following the June 21 election victory of Colombia’s new reactionary President Abelardo de la Espriella, outgoing President Gustavo Petro attributed leftist candidate Ivan Cepeda’s defeat to a plague of bots and internet-borne disinformation. The source, he suggested, was the Israeli cyber-intelligence company BlackCore. Now, however, Petro relies on the forensic analysis of Fernando Cerimedo’s phone. It suggests he collaborated with Colombian electoral officials. Cerimedo refers to “more than two million bots and fake profiles managed by automated farms operating from abroad and the city of Medellín.” Petro called for annulment of the election results and recently repeated the accusations in an interview with Mexico’s La Jornada newspaper. In Argentina and Brazil Cerimedo also meddled in elections in Argentina. According to Beller, President Javier Milei paid Cerimedo $800,000 USD per month to carry out online disinformation. Serving as chief technology and communications officer for Milei’s successful campaign in 2023, he secured large donations and expanded his social media capabilities. Cerimedo admitted to La Nación newspaper that year that, “He controls ‘farms’ of thousands of trolls, bot accounts, and other digital tools put into service for Milei’s party.” He exercised his technical and digital capabilities, and his scheming, in Brazil, too. Cerimedo joined Jair Bolsonaro’s presidential campaigns and provided assistance to Bolsonaro’s failed coup attempt that ended in January 2023. Bolsonaro’s son, Eduardo, now living in Florida, in February 2026 hosted the “Hispanic Prosperity Gala” held at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. Argentine President Milei delivered the keynote address, and Eduardo Bolsonaro presented Cerimedo with an award honoring him as the “Hispanic Political Consultant of the Year.” Cast of characters On being honored at the Mar-a-Lago Gala, Cerimedo began by saying that, “I want to say something in English; thank you to Brad Parscale!” U.S. operative Parscale had tutored Cerimedo in the uses of social media, trolls, bots, and algorithms for electioneering purposes. The latter told The New York Times that, “Brad set up all the infrastructure that I work with.” Their partnership continued. Parscale worked for Trump, serving as digital media director for his 2016 presidential campaign and campaign manager for part of his 2020 re-election effort. Cerimedo’s collaboration with the well-connected Parscale may have allowed him to make connections of his own. Cerimedo partnered with the Argentinian-American Damián Merlo. This lobbyist owner of the Miami-based Latin America Advisory Group (LAAG) had worked at the U.S. Interests Section in Havana and as program officer at the interventionist International Republican Institute. Cerimedo’s connection to Merlo’s LAAG lobbying group provided him with indirect access to the Florida congressional delegation and to executive branch officials responsible for Latin America. The duo formed the Numen publicity company, which undertook efforts to generate U.S. support for Milei’s presidential campaign in Argentina in 2023. They shaped publicity for the U.S. and advocated for Milei among members of the U.S. Congress and the media. As noted by the Cubadebate Media Observatory, “Cerimedo built a corporate base in Miami and a transnational media network. The U.S. would be its center of operations. It benefited from privileged links with the top power structures within the Trump administration, in particular with Marco Rubio.” After Milei’s electoral win, the Numen organization, helped along by Parscale’s technical help and his travel to Bolivia, played important roles in the 2025 electoral victories of Paz in Bolivia and Asfura in Honduras. Numen also appears as an “academy” offering “digital and political marketing courses” in the region. Cerimedo and two Argentinian journalists formed La Derecho Diario (Daily of the Right) prior to 2020. It’s a widely-read, pan-Hispanic source of news and views with a reactionary slant; there’s an English-language version. A recent story titled “Wave of Moroccan immigrants arrives in Brazil thanks to Lula” typifies its deceptive content. The Spanish impresario Javier Negre, a “megaphone” for the far-right Vox political party, owns his own far-right media conglomerate, and in 2024, he purchased 50% interest in Cerimedo’s La Derecho Diario and took over as director. With Cerimedo now in trouble, though, he’s abandoned the platform. Loose ends On his digital rampage across Latin America, Cerimedo was a prominent soldier in a war being carried out by Latin America’s extreme right wing. He and others built a network of media and digital communications to serve the wealthy and politically powerful in Latin America. Cerimedo found friends and supporters in Washington and in southern Florida, hotbed of emigre agitation. The U.S. government has likely provided more substantial support for his activities, but further details are so far scarce. Evo Morales, the former Bolivian president ousted in a U.S.-supported coup in 2019, claims Cerimedo was working for the CIA. Cerimedo’s former partner Beller says likewise. Lots of money cropped up along his path, as noted above, that may signal official U.S. involvement. The U.S. government directs vast sums to “national security,” a category that historically included undercover activities of all kinds. It’s conceivable that some of Cerimedo’s projects could have been classified as such. A report appearing on ciudadano.com on Aug. 27 is relevant in this regard. Investigators looking at Cerimedo’s mobile phone found “codes linked to a network of digital wallets.” The report refers to a “cold wallet” allowing for “the discreet transfer of large sums of money.” Investigators discovered “transactions totaling $44,100…over the last six months.” More shocking, though? They “uncovered accounts handling staggering sums, including one that holds $132 million.” We hope you appreciated this article. content: US investment firm Susquehanna International Group has agreed to lease more than 4,808 square metres (51,762 square feet) of office space at the Cheung Kong Center II, a prime office skyscraper developed by CK Asset Holdings in Hong Kong’s main business zone of Central, according to market sources. title: Markets decline amid West Asia conflict, concerns over possible US interest-rate hike
content: MUMBAI: Stock market benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty drifted lower in early trade on Monday as elevated crude oil prices, escalation in US-Iran hostilities and concerns over a possible US interest rate hike weighed on investors' sentiment. The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 172.77 points to 76,342.66 in early trade. The 50-share NSE Nifty declined 63.30 points to 23,832.60. Among the 30 Sensex firms, Infosys, Tech Mahindra, HCL Tech, Tata Steel, Tata Consultancy Services and UltraTech Cement were among the major laggards. Eternal, Bharti Airtel, Bharat Electronics and Larsen & Toubro were among the winners. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, traded 0.78 per cent higher at USD 97 per barrel. "Friday's US jobs report came in far stronger than expected, reviving concerns over a possible interest-rate hike, while fresh attacks in the US-Iran conflict are keeping oil prices at elevated levels, posing a key overhang for domestic investor sentiment," Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder & CEO of HST Wealth, a research analyst firm, said. The next major catalyst comes on Friday with the release of US inflation data, which is expected to influence Federal Reserve rate expectations and, consequently, global risk sentiment, he added. In Asian markets, South Korea's Kospi jumped 3.36 per cent, Japan's Nikkei 225 index climbed 1.83 per cent. Shanghai's SSE Composite index and Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was trading lower.

title: Sensex, Nifty Fall In Early Trade As Crude Prices, US-Iran Tensions Weigh
content: Stock market benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty drifted lower in early trade on Monday as elevated crude oil prices, escalation in US-Iran hostilities and concerns over a possible US interest rate hike weighed on investors' sentiment.The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 172.77 points to 76,342.66 in early trade. The 50-share NSE Nifty declined 63.30 points to 23,832.60. Among the 30 Sensex firms, Infosys, Tech Mahindra, HCL Tech, Tata Steel, Tata Consultancy Services and UltraTech Cement were among the major laggards. Eternal, Bharti Airtel, Bharat Electronics and Larsen & Toubro were among the winners. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, traded 0.78 per cent higher at USD 97 per barrel. "Friday's US jobs report came in far stronger than expected, reviving concerns over a possible interest-rate hike, while fresh attacks in the US-Iran conflict are keeping oil prices at elevated levels, posing a key overhang for domestic investor sentiment," Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder & CEO of HST Wealth, a research analyst firm, said. The next major catalyst comes on Friday with the release of US inflation data, which is expected to influence Federal Reserve rate expectations and, consequently, global risk sentiment, he added. In Asian markets, South Korea's Kospi jumped 3.36 per cent, Japan's Nikkei 225 index climbed 1.83 per cent. Shanghai's SSE Composite index and Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was trading lower. US markets ended in negative territory on Friday. "Crude oil remains the dominant macro driver. WTI continues to trade at elevated levels around USD 91–92 per barrel as the latest escalation in US-Iran hostilities around the Strait of Hormuz keeps concerns over potential supply disruptions firmly in focus," Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, an online trading and wealth-tech firm, said. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) offloaded equities worth Rs 3,111.94 crore on Friday, according to exchange data. On Friday, the Sensex climbed 362.57 points, or 0.48 per cent, to settle at 76,515.43. The Nifty, however, saw a modest rise of 24.25 points, or 0.10 per cent, to end at 23,897.70.

title: AcroMeta to Enter Ambient Temperature Cellular Logistics Through Strategic Partnership with Macro HRD SG Pte. Ltd. – IT Business Net
content: AcroMeta to acquire a strategic stake in Macro-ATCLS Pte. Ltd., for the Ambient Temperature Cellular Logistics business. Option to acquire an exclusive licence to deploy the Ambient Temperature Cellular Logistics platform across Southeast Asia. The Group will continue to evaluate strategic opportunities that support its long-term growth. [L-R] Signing ceremony between Mr Toh Ker How, Executive Director of AcroMeta Group Limited, and Ms Kawinyarat Mardpiratchata, CFO and Managing Partner of Macro-HRD Pte. Ltd. SINGAPORE, Sept 7, 2026 – (ACN Newswire) – AcroMeta Group Limited (“AcroMeta”, or the “Company”, and together with its subsidiaries, the “Group”) today announced that it has entered into a non-binding term sheet (“Term Sheet”) with Macro HRD SG Pte. Ltd. (“Macro”), a Singapore-based provider of management consultancy services to the healthcare sector. The Term Sheet sets out the principal terms for a strategic partnership between AcroMeta and Macro-ATCLS Pte. Ltd. (“Macro-ATCLS”), the company through which Macro’s Ambient Temperature Cellular Logistics technology is being commercialised. Mr Lawrence Toh, Executive Director of AcroMeta Group Limited, said, “This proposed strategic partnership gives us the opportunity to build a position in an industry where cell and gene therapy logistics are expected to grow at double-digit rates in the years ahead. We see this as a natural extension of our strategy to grow our portfolio beyond our core operations, and we’re excited about the potential to build a meaningful presence in bringing this technology into Southeast Asia.” About Ambient Temperature Cellular Logistics (ATCLS) Ambient Temperature Cell Logistics (ATCLS) is an emerging technology licensed by Macro HRD, designed to fundamentally transform the transportation and distribution of living cells and other temperature-sensitive biological materials by eliminating reliance on conventional refrigerated and cryogenic cold chains. ATCLS uses proprietary ambient-temperature preservation and reactivation technologies, supported by its proprietary Gradient Equilibrium Decision Modeling (GEDM) platform for real-time governance, chain-of-identity and process control, enabling dormant living cells to be transported at ambient temperature and reactivated at the point of use. The opportunity addresses rapidly expanding markets including stem cells, CAR-T/immune-cell therapy, gene therapy, regenerative medicine, organ and tissue transplantation, and cell-and-gene-therapy logistics; the underlying markets cited in the project materials range from US$5.2 billion for immune-cell therapy to US$47 billion for organ transplantation, while the global cell-and-gene-therapy 3PL market is estimated at US$1.81 billion in 2025 and projected to reach US$16.95 billion by 2035 (25.1% CAGR). Based on defined ambient-addressable segments, ATCLS estimates a Serviceable Addressable Market (SAM) of approximately US$14.5 billion by 2032, positioning the technology as a potential category-creating solution capable of reducing the cost, fragility and geographic limitations of conventional cold-chain logistics. (See Footnote 1) Proposed Exclusive Licensing Arrangement for Southeast Asia AcroMeta will have an option to acquire an exclusive licence to deploy the ATCLS technology across agreed territories in Southeast Asia, including the right to appoint sub-licensees. The proposed exclusive licensing arrangement is intended to provide AcroMeta with the rights to develop and commercialise the ATCLS business within Southeast Asia. This structure allows AcroMeta to secure exclusive rights across the Southeast Asian markets, together with a first right to acquire additional territories, significantly expanding the Group’s potential commercial reach for the ATCLS technology. Building AcroMeta’s Platform Growth Strategy The Group intends to continue evaluating strategic opportunities to support its long-term value creation for shareholders. The Board remains focused on disciplined capital allocation as the Group progresses through its next phase of development. Footnote 1: This information was provided by Macro’s management and has not been verified by the board of directors. The directors have not audited or verified the data supplied by the company. About AcroMeta Group Limited (SGX: 43F) AcroMeta Group Limited (“AcroMeta” or the “Company”, and together with its subsidiaries, the “Group”), is in the business of facility management services. The Company has been listed on the Catalist board of the Singapore Exchange since 2016. For more information, please visit www.AcroMeta.com. About Macro HRD SG Pte. Ltd. (Macro HRD) Macro HRD is a Singapore-based biotechnology and therapeutics company established in 2024, focused on developing scalable, precision-medicine solutions for high-burden infectious diseases with significant unmet medical needs. The company integrates advanced biology, therapeutic platform technologies and AI/ML-enabled decision systems to accelerate drug discovery and translational development from scientific research through clinical application. Its development portfolio includes innovative approaches targeting HIV/AIDS, HPV and other enveloped viruses, supported by proprietary therapeutic and drug-delivery platforms. Macro HRD brings together an international network of scientific, clinical, regulatory, investment and technology expertise, with the mission of translating breakthrough science into novel therapeutics with meaningful global healthcare impact.
